key: helmets slow batters down, real pros
name: ch07_helmet_commentators
alt: Two cricket commentators argue opposite extremes about helmets while a batter calmly picks the helmet based on the bowler.
scene: A wide view of a local cricket ground on a sunny afternoon, seen from beside a small wooden commentary box with two microphones. Inside the box on the left sits a loud commentator in a striped polo shirt, leaning back with arms spread wide, one hand waving a helmet away, a speech bubble showing a helmet crossed out. On the right a second commentator in a blazer and tie leans forward, pointing urgently, his speech bubble showing a batter wrapped head to toe in comically huge armour like a knight. Down on the pitch in the centre, a young batter in whites stands at the crease calmly holding a helmet in one hand and looking down the pitch at the bowler. Two small inset circles near the batter show the choice: in one a gentle slow spinner tossing the ball softly, with the helmet resting on the ground beside the batter; in the other a fast bowler mid-run with a bouncer flying head-high, and the helmet firmly on. The batter's face is relaxed and thoughtful, not scared, not reckless. A scoreboard and a few spectators under a neem tree fill the background. In a faint corner, a tiny invisible-looking ball drawn only as a dotted outline hints that some dangers cannot be seen coming. Clear daylight, light-hearted mood. Labels: "BOTH EXAGGERATE" above the commentary box, and "DEPENDS ON THE BOWLER" under the batter.

key: on a pressure cooker is a precise standard
name: ch07_premium_chips_label
alt: A shopper trusts the precise certification mark on a pressure cooker but has to turn over a chips packet labelled premium to read what is really inside.
scene: A bright aisle in a neighbourhood supermarket, shown as a split illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same shopper in both halves: a woman in her 30s in a green salwar kameez with a cloth shopping bag on her shoulder. LEFT panel: she holds up a shiny steel pressure cooker and looks satisfied; a crisp round certification stamp on the cooker's side, drawn as a plain seal with a tick inside (no real logo), is magnified in an inset circle with a measuring ruler and a gauge needle, suggesting a precise, tested standard. RIGHT panel: she holds a puffy packet of potato chips whose front shows a big glossy ribbon badge with sparkles; she has turned the packet over and squints at a long block of tiny ingredient lines on the back through a magnifying glass, eyebrows raised. A small inset shows four short rows on the back of the packet, marked A, C, I and D: rows A and D are crisp and clear, row I is blurry and smudged, and row C is faint and greyed out, as if it barely belongs there. Shelves of spice tins and biscuit packets behind her, fluorescent store lighting, mildly amused mood. Labels: "PRECISE" at the top of the left panel, "PREMIUM?" on the chips packet's badge, and "READ THE BACK" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch07_unread_badge_mismatch
alt: A phone chat list shows an unread counter of zero beside a chat with a bold new message, and a puzzled person spots the mismatch.
scene: A close, eye-level view of a young man in his 20s in a grey hoodie sitting on a bus seat by the window, holding his phone at chest height and frowning at it, one eyebrow raised. The phone is enlarged as a big inset filling the centre of the picture: a generic chat app (no logos) with a list of three chats, each with a round avatar circle. The top chat row has a bold message preview and a fresh time stamp, clearly new, yet the green round counter badge next to it plainly reads "0". Two thin arrows point from the bold message and from the badge towards each other, meeting at a small orange exclamation badge in between, showing that the two things disagree. Below the phone, a small diagram shows the idea behind it: two separate index cards on a table, one card holding the message and one card holding the unread count, with a dotted link between them broken in the middle; one card was updated, the other was not yet. Outside the bus window, a blur of shops and an auto-rickshaw passing in afternoon sunlight. The other passengers are faint background shapes. Calm, slightly puzzled mood. Labels: "NEW MESSAGE" beside the bold chat row, and "COUNT SAYS 0" beside the green badge, both short and placed outside the phone frame with thin pointer lines.

key: is a single-lane bridge: only one vehicle at a time
name: ch07_single_lane_vs_roundabout
alt: A single-lane bridge lets one vehicle cross at a time safely but slowly, while a busy roundabout keeps traffic moving with an occasional small bump.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing Indian road traffic from a slightly raised angle. LEFT panel: a narrow single-lane bridge over a small river, with a single scooter crossing it, its rider in a yellow helmet. On the near bank a calm traffic policeman in a white shirt and cap holds up his palm, and behind him a long patient queue of vehicles waits in a line: an auto-rickshaw, a car, a tempo, a cyclist. A small hourglass floats above the queue. Everyone is perfectly safe, nothing touches, but the line is long. A green shield with a tick hovers over the bridge. RIGHT panel: a busy roundabout with a small garden island in the middle and a few painted arrows on the road; cars, auto-rickshaws and two-wheelers flow around it smoothly and quickly. At one entry point, a small car and an auto-rickshaw have just bumped gently, a little star-shaped bump mark between them and both drivers leaning out with surprised faces, nothing serious. A tiny orange exclamation badge marks the bump. Midday sunlight, trees along the road, lively but friendly mood. Labels: "SERIALIZABLE" at the top of the left panel, and "WEAK ISOLATION" at the top of the right panel.

key: on a slightly delayed stream that you started
name: ch07_delayed_stream_scoreboard
alt: A viewer watches a cricket match on a delayed stream frozen at the moment he joined, while the live stadium has already moved on.
scene: A split illustration showing two places at the same instant. LEFT: a cosy living room where a young man in a T-shirt and shorts sits cross-legged on a sofa with a bowl of popcorn, watching cricket on a laptop on the coffee table. The laptop screen shows a scoreboard with a simple score and a small wall-clock icon reading three o'clock, the moment he started watching. On his screen a small umpire signal shows a review still pending, with a question mark. A wall clock behind him shows a later time, a few minutes past three. RIGHT: the real stadium, bright and loud, where the review has already been decided: the big stadium screen shows a red cross for out, a fielder celebrates with arms raised, and the crowd in the stands cheers. A long dashed arrow runs from the stadium towards the laptop with a small hourglass on it, showing the news has not reached his screen yet. Between the two halves, a camera-shutter icon over the laptop suggests his view is a frozen picture of the moment he joined. The young man looks relaxed and unaware, the stadium is full of motion. Afternoon light in both scenes. Labels: "AS OF 3:00" above the laptop, and "LIVE" above the stadium screen.

key: each saved version is a whole document you can open
name: ch07_doc_versions_shared_paras
alt: Several saved versions of one document look like whole copies, but behind them unchanged paragraphs are shared cards and only changed paragraphs are new.
scene: A clean, diagram-like illustration of a desk with a filing tray, seen from the front. At the top, three document folders stand in a row like tabs, labelled with small tags "v10", "v11" and "v12", each opening to look like a complete document. A young woman in a teal kurta and spectacles stands at the right, pointing at the folder tagged "v12" and opening it with interest. Below the folders, on the desk surface, lies a single shared pool of paragraph cards: about six rectangular cards with grey text lines. Thin coloured strings run down from each folder to the cards it uses: most strings from all three folders converge on the same few grey cards, showing the paragraphs are shared and not copied, while each newer folder also has one string to its own fresh amber card holding a changed paragraph. The strings from v12 are drawn slightly bolder, starting at a small round knob on the folder, like a root. In the lower left corner, a small paper shredder with a broom beside it hints that a database sweeps away old folders nobody is reading anymore, while a tiny archive box beside it suggests the document app keeps all history. Soft office light, tidy and calm mood. Labels: "ROOT 12" next to the knob on the v12 folder, and "SHARED" over the pool of grey paragraph cards.

key: at three different restaurants: same words
name: ch07_medium_spicy_three_dhabas
alt: Three restaurants serve dishes labelled medium spicy, and a taster finds each one has wildly different heat.
scene: A wide street scene with three small restaurants side by side, each with its own awning: a South Indian tiffin hall in green on the left, a Punjabi dhaba in orange in the middle, and an Andhra meals mess in red on the right. In front of each, on a small table, sits one bowl of curry with an identical little paper flag reading "MEDIUM". Above each bowl hovers a simple chilli meter with a needle: on the left almost no heat with one small chilli, in the middle two chillies, and on the right the needle slammed into the red with flames curling out. A young food lover in a cap and a backpack walks along the row with a steel spoon, tasting. At the left table he smiles calmly; at the middle table he fans his mouth a little; at the right table he is red-faced, eyes watering, gulping from a glass of water, with tiny steam puffs coming out of his ears. A waiter in an apron stands at the right restaurant, shrugging with an innocent smile and pointing at the same word on the menu. Bright evening light with string bulbs over the awnings, comic mood. Labels: "SAME WORDS" above the three flags, and "TASTE TO KNOW" near the young man at the right.
